cita: Lu et al. (2025). ViDove: A Translation Agent System with Multimodal Context and Memory-Augmented Reasoning.
problema: Multimodal video subtitling/translation agents must fuse visual, audio and textual cues coherently across long documents, but most LLM-based MT systems only handle text and lose domain/visual context across chunks.
mecanismo: A short-term memory Ms (per-video-chunk translation history, visual/audio cues) and long-term memory Ml (domain knowledge, web knowledge via Tavily) are implemented over LlamaIndex; three collaborating agents (Translator, Proofreader, Editor) write, consolidate and retrieve from M during multi-agent post-editing.
evaluacion: Evaluated on DoveBench (17h human-annotated long-form video) and BigVideo using BLEU/BLEURT/SubER/SubSONAR/sCOMET against Gemini-2.5-Flash, Qwen-2.5-Omni, VideoCaptioner and Whisper+DelTA, plus an ablation removing domain memory, vision and the proofreader agent.
numeros_clave: vs strongest baseline Whisper+DelTA: +28.8% BLEU, +58.9% BLEURT, -15.5% SubER (DoveBench); ablation Table 2: full ViDove BLEU 15.84 vs w/o domain memory 14.86 vs w/o Proofreader 13.56 (sharpest drop).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The ablation (Table 2, Sec 5.4) measures retrieval-relevant memory components (domain memory, vision) directly against BLEU/SubER, confirming MF's practice of gating memory design on measured retrieval outcomes.
Long/short-term memory split reduces re-processing cost of prior chunks (Sec 3.5.1) but no explicit token/latency numbers are reported, so it is only weak context for MF's cost lens.

notes: Ablation numbers at Table 2 (Sec 5.4, single-column DoveBench subset); main comparison Table 1 (Sec 5.3).

cita: Yan et al. (2025). General Agentic Memory Via Deep Research.
problema: Ahead-of-time (AOT) static memory precompresses agent history offline and is inevitably lossy and inflexible to unforeseen, fine-grained downstream requests at retrieval time.
mecanismo: A duo design follows just-in-time compilation: a Memorizer writes a lightweight memo per session while keeping the full trajectory in a page-store; a Researcher performs iterative plan/search/reflect deep-research (vector, BM25 and ID-based tools) over the page-store guided by the memo to build a task-specific context at runtime, trained end-to-end via RL.
evaluacion: Benchmarked on LoCoMo, HotpotQA (56K/224K/448K), RULER-128K and NarrativeQA against memory-free (long-LLM, RAG) and memory-based baselines (A-Mem, Mem0, MemoryOS, LightMem), with ablations on search tools, module isolation, output format and offline/online efficiency timing.
numeros_clave: HotpotQA-56K F1: GAM 64.07 vs best baseline LightMem 37.30; module ablation (Table 3) 'memory without research' collapses to avg F1 27.50 vs full GAM 53.18; efficiency (Table 5) GAM total time 69.32s at 56K vs A-mem 210.26s, though costlier online than Mem0 (37.57s) or LightMem (5.13s).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The 'memory without research' ablation (Table 3, Sec 3.5) shows a precomputed static memory alone underperforms sharply, confirming MF's stance of treating any derived/compressed index as a cache and re-deriving/searching over ground truth rather than trusting it standalone.

Table 5 (Sec 3.6) measures offline-build vs online-serve latency directly, giving a concrete cost/accuracy tradeoff curve (GAM slower online than Mem0/LightMem for higher F1) relevant to MF's context-economy lens, without forcing a specific MF decision.

notes: Ablation tables 3 (module isolation) and 5 (efficiency) in Sec 3.5-3.6; ranked accuracy tables 1-2 in Sec 3.2-3.3.

cita: Fiorini et al. (2025). Episodic Memory in Agentic Frameworks: Suggesting Next Tasks.
problema: Scientific-workflow agentic frameworks need to recommend plausible next steps without relying on hallucination-prone pre-trained LLM guesses or costly fine-tuning on scarce proprietary workflow data.
mecanismo: An Episodic-Memory (EM) Agent intercepts user instructions, compiles the executed trajectory into a ProvLake/W3C-PROV workflow, retrieves similar past workflows via tree matching plus embedding similarity of leaf steps from a workflow database, and asks an LLM to suggest next tasks from the retrieved and current workflows; a '\save' command explicitly writes the current workflow back into episodic memory.
evaluacion: Demonstrated qualitatively (no quantitative benchmark) on a Materials-Science PFAS-hazard-assessment crew built with BeeAI, using illustrative execution traces (with vs without a retrievable similar workflow) with similarity threshold T=0.65 and up to 10 retrieved workflows.
numeros_clave: similarity threshold T=0.65; max 10 retrieved workflows per query (Sec 3, implementation paragraph); no quantitative accuracy/latency figures are reported (evidence is CUALITATIVA).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The core mechanism stores past executed workflows (ordered task sequences) as plan-state memory and matches the in-progress workflow against them to suggest next steps (Sec 2, Fig. 1b) -- a concrete pattern MF could adopt for plan-state-as-memory.

Retrieval uses a fixed similarity threshold and tree matching (Sec 2) but is validated only through illustrative examples, not a measured benchmark, so it is weak (qualitative-only) evidence for MF's retrieval-measured discipline.

notes: Only qualitative demonstration (Figs. 3-4, Sec 3); RECONSIDERAR -- evidence is illustrative-only, no quantitative retrieval or task-suggestion accuracy is reported.

cita: Zou et al. (2026). Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems.
problema: Text-mediated multi-agent collaboration re-encodes each agent's reasoning into natural language, which is lossy relative to the model's internal representations and imposes heavy token and latency costs on system-level reasoning.
mecanismo: Each agent autoregressively generates 'latent thoughts' as last-layer hidden states instead of decoding text, and a shared latent working memory (concatenated layer-wise KV caches, with a training-free linear alignment operator) transfers this state losslessly to the next agent, replacing token-level write/read of memory with continuous-representation write/read across agents.
evaluacion: Evaluated on 9 benchmarks (math/science reasoning, commonsense, code generation) across 5 backbones (Qwen3 4B/8B/14B, Llama3 3B/8B) under sequential and hierarchical MAS designs, against single-model and text-based MAS (TextMAS, vLLM-optimized) baselines.
numeros_clave: up to +14.6% accuracy, 70.8%-83.7% fewer output tokens, and 4x-4.3x faster end-to-end inference vs TextMAS (Sec 4.1); e.g. Qwen3-14B sequential MedQA: 80.7% acc with 86.6% fewer tokens and 4.3x speedup over TextMAS (Table 1-2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Measured 70.8-83.7% token reduction and 4-4.3x speedup from replacing textual inter-agent memory with shared latent KV-cache state (Fig. 1, Table 1-2) is a concrete mechanism MF could borrow for internal, non-human-facing agent-to-agent handoffs to cut context/token cost.

Theorem 3.3 (Sec 3.2) proves the latent transfer is information-lossless relative to text hand-off, a fidelity argument that is internal to the model rather than about human-auditable provenance, so it only weakly bears on MF's fidelity/staleness concerns.

notes: Complexity/expressiveness proofs in Appendix B (Theorems 3.1, 3.3, 3.4); main efficiency numbers Fig. 1 and Tables 1-2, Sec 4.1-4.2.

cita: Liao et al. (2026). From Atom to Community: Structured and Evolving Agent Memory for User Behavior Modeling.
problema: Single, unstructured summary memories for user-behavior modeling conflate multi-dimensional interests, suffer interest-forgetting from naive overwriting, and cannot exploit collaborative signals from similar users under sparse interaction data.
mecanismo: STEAM decomposes user preferences into fine-grained atomic memory units (content, embedding, linked interactions, community link); relation extraction plus 2-hop BFS groups semantically similar memories across users into communities summarized as prototype memories (graph representation), and reflection-triggered consolidation (merge overlapping memories) or formation (new memory unit) evolve memory over time.
evaluacion: Evaluated on three real-world recommendation datasets (Amazon CDs, Clothing, MovieLens-100k, 100 sampled users) via NDCG@{1,5,10} recommendation accuracy, user-simulation fidelity (F1) against GPT-3.5/AFL, diversity metrics (ILD/Entropy/DS), and an ablation removing atomic memory units (AMU), consolidation (MC) or community construction (CC).
numeros_clave: overall NDCG improvement of +5.74% over the best baseline (Table 2); ablation on CDs (Table 5) NDCG@10: full STEAM 0.5982 vs w/o AMU 0.5765, w/o MC 0.5886, w/o CC 0.5906.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The consolidation-vs-formation evolution mechanism (Sec 3.4, Table 5 ablation) gives a concrete, measured pattern for merging overlapping memories into refined units, which MF's gotcha-to-recipe consolidation could adopt directly.

Table 5's ablation isolates the retrieval-relevant community-construction component and measures its NDCG contribution (0.5906 vs 0.5982 full), confirming MF's discipline of gating structure on measured retrieval gains rather than assumed benefit.

notes: Ablation Table 5 (Sec 4.5); main NDCG comparison Table 2 (Sec 4.2.2).

cita: Charoenwet et al. (2026). AgenticSCR: An Autonomous Agentic Secure Code Review for Immature Vulnerabilities Detection.
problema: Pre-commit secure code review of 'immature' (incomplete, context-dependent) vulnerabilities is poorly served by noisy rule-based SAST tools and by standalone LLMs that lack repository context and explicit tool use.
mecanismo: A detector-validator subagent chain writes curated SAST rule knowledge (CodeQL-derived, CWE-mapped JSON) into the detector's semantic memory and a CWE-tree knowledge base into the validator's semantic memory; the detector localizes/explains vulnerabilities from a diff-centric view of the repo, and the validator recalls the CWE tree to filter false positives from the detector's candidate comments.
evaluacion: Evaluated on SCRBench, a curated repository-aware human-annotated line-level immature-vulnerability benchmark, against a static LLM baseline and SAST tools, with an ablation toggling security knowledge (SAST/CWE) in the detector and validator subagents versus a 'Vanilla Agentic' baseline.
numeros_clave: 17.5% of comments correctly localized/relevant/typed, +10.6 absolute points over the static LLM baseline while producing only 32% as many comments; ablation: full security-knowledge config raises absolute localization/relevance rate by +10.2 points over Vanilla Agentic with 81% fewer comments; abstract cites >=153% relative improvement in correct comments over the static-LLM baseline.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Grounding the detector/validator in curated documentary knowledge (SAST rule JSON, CWE tree, Sec 3.4.1) rather than relying on the LLM's implicit pretrained knowledge measurably improves precision, confirming MF's docs-as-verified-truth principle.

The ablation (Sec 1, contributions) directly measures the retrieval/use of security knowledge against localization+relevance rate, aligning with MF's requirement that retrieval value be measured, not assumed.

notes: Ablation numbers reported in abstract/introduction (Sec 1); SCRBench described in Sec 2-3.
